'''Dame Juliet Ann Gerrard''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|DNZM|FRSNZ}} (born 1967) is a New Zealand biochemistry academic. She is a professor at the [[University of Auckland]]<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/people/j-gerrard |title=Professor Juliet Gerrard – The University of Auckland |publisher=Unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz |access-date=9 April 2018}}</ref> and was New Zealand [[Prime Minister's Chief Science Advisor]] during the administration of [[Jacinda Ardern]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juliet Gerrard |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/juliet/ |access-date=2024-12-05 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Gerrard was born in [[Nottingham]], [[Nottinghamshire]], England, in 1967.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.sbs.auckland.ac.nz/en/about/news-and-events/news/news-2014/2014/professor-juliet-gerrard--a-protein-packed-life.html |title=Professor Juliet Gerrard: A protein-packed life |date=18 November 2014 |publisher=University of Auckland |access-date=18 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.freebmd.org.uk/cgi/information.pl?cite=fQ4k1ne5NNbDdBUcm3%2BJFg&scan=1 |title=Index entry |access-date=12 June 2021 |work=FreeBMD |publisher=ONS}}</ref> Her family frequently moved around the United Kingdom when she was a child, living in various locations including [[Nottingham]], [[Wales]] and [[Grimsby]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Easther|first=Elisabeth|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12327773|title=My Story: Dr Juliet Gerrard - The life and times of the Prime Minister's Chief Science Advisor|date=2020-04-27|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=2020-04-28|language=en-NZ|issn=1170-0777}}</ref> She liked science and focused on chemistry in her studies.<ref name=":0" />

==Education and career==
Gerrard obtained a [[British undergraduate degree classification#First-class honours|first-class honours degree]] in chemistry at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name=Update>{{cite magazine |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Our 2018 Honorary Fellows |magazine=Update |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry |date=April 2019 }}</ref> and then in 1992 a [[DPhil]]<ref name=Update/> titled ''Studies on dihydrodipicolinate synthase'', also from Oxford.<ref name=Cantab>{{cite web |url= http://www.canterbury.ac.nz/science/contact-us/people/juliet-gerrard.html |title=Science Staff Profiles &#124; University of Canterbury |publisher=Canterbury.ac.nz |date=12 October 2017 |access-date=9 April 2018}}</ref>  She moved to [[New Zealand Institute for Crop and Food Research|Crop and Food]] in New Zealand in 1997<ref name="RNZ new advisor">{{cite news |last1=Scotcher |first1=Katie |title=Juliet Gerrard named as Chief Science Advisor |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/359448/juliet-gerrard-named-as-chief-science-advisor |access-date=24 July 2019 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=12 June 2018}}</ref> and then the [[University of Canterbury]] in 1998, where she rose to full professor.<ref name=Cantab/> She then moved to a professorship at the [[University of Auckland]] in 2014,<ref name="RNZ new advisor" /> where she holds a Callaghan Innovation Industry and Outreach Fellowship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://macdiarmid.ac.nz/member/gerrard-juliet/ |title=Professor Juliet Gerrard – MacDiarmid Institute |publisher=Macdiarmid.ac.nz |date=6 August 2015 |access-date=9 April 2018}}</ref> Having been the recipient of [[Marsden grant]]s herself in 1998 and 2003, Gerrard went on to serve as the chair of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]]'s Marsden Fund Council from 2012 until 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1711/S00008/846m-in-marsden-funding-for-nz-researchers.htm |title=$84.6m in Marsden funding for NZ researchers &#124; Scoop News |publisher=Scoop.co.nz |date=2 November 2017 |access-date=9 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://macdiarmid.ac.nz/juliet-gerrard-new-chair-of-marsden-fund-council/|title=Juliet Gerrard new Chair of Marsden Fund Council|date=24 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.newshub.co.nz/nznews/this-years-marsden-fund-recipients-revealed-2014110410|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170423103059/http://www.newshub.co.nz/nznews/this-years-marsden-fund-recipients-revealed-2014110410|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 April 2017|title=This year's Marsden Fund recipients revealed|newspaper=[[Newshub]] |date=11 March 2014|via=www.newshub.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Chair of the Marsden Fund Council|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/funds/marsden/about/council/gerrard/ |access-date=17 October 2013}}</ref>

Her research includes investigations of protein-protein interactions, [[lysine]] [[biosynthesis]] (particularly the enzyme [[dihydrodipicolinate synthase]]) and the application of protein chemistry to the food industry.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Gerrard|first=Juliet|title=Protein–protein crosslinking in food: methods, consequences, applications|journal=Trends in Food Science and Technology|year=2002|volume=13|issue=12|pages=391–399|doi=10.1016/s0924-2244(02)00257-1}}</ref><ref name="pmid17579770">{{cite journal |vauthors=Hutton CA, Perugini MA, Gerrard JA |title=Inhibition of lysine biosynthesis: an evolving antibiotic strategy. |journal=Mol Biosyst |volume=3 |issue=7 |pages=458–65 |year=2007 |pmid=17579770 |doi=10.1039/b705624a}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Gerrard|first=J|author2=SE Fayle |author3=AJ Wilson |author4=MP Newberry |author5=M Ross |author6=S Kavale |title=Dough properties and crumb strength of white pan bread as affected by microbial transglutaminase|journal=Journal of Food Science|year=1998|volume=63|issue=3|pages=472–475|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2621.1998.tb15766.x}}</ref>  She has over 175 publications, including three books.<ref name=Update/>

In June 2018 she was appointed the [[Prime Minister of New Zealand|New Zealand Prime Minister]]'s Chief Science Advisor, succeeding [[Peter Gluckman|Sir Peter Gluckman]]<ref>{{cite news |title=PM Jacinda Ardern announces new science advisor |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/104642064/pm-jacinda-ardern-announces-new-science-advisor |newspaper=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=12 June 2018 |access-date=13 June 2018}}</ref> and taking up the role for two three-year terms starting 1 July 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=New PM's Chief Science Advisor – Expert reaction |url= http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/SC1806/S00026/new-pms-chief-science-advisor-expert-reaction.htm |newspaper=Scoop |date=12 June 2018 |access-date=13 June 2018}}</ref> In her role she has tried to "draw on as many science voices as possible", and to be "rigorous, transparent, accessible and inclusive".<ref name=":0" />

== Honours and awards ==
In 2004, Gerrard won a National Teaching Award for Sustained Excellence in Teaching.<ref name="Update" /> In 2012, she was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref name="FRSNZ">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/g-i/|title=List of all Fellows with surnames G-I|date=2017|website=royalsociety.org.nz|publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand|access-date=6 April 2019}}</ref> In 2018, she was made an Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name="Update" /> 

In the [[2021 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2021 New Year Honours]], Gerrard was appointed a [[Dame Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to science.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/new-year-honours-list-2021 |title=New Year honours list 2021 |date=31 December 2020 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=31 December 2020}}</ref> In 2017, Gerrard was selected as one of the Royal Society Te Apārangi's "[[150 women in 150 words]]", celebrating the contributions of women to knowledge in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Juliet Gerrard|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/juliet/|access-date=2021-05-10|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>

==Other==
She has a [[koru]] tattoo on her back, purchased for by her lab group for being made professor before her fortieth birthday.<ref name=tat>{{cite news|title=Ninth International London Tattoo Convention|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/features/culture/ninth-international-london-tattoo-convention/2007544.article|access-date=17 October 2013}}</ref>

She has spun out her own company called Hi-Aspect, which produces protein [[Nanofiber|nanofibres]] for medical and other uses.<ref name=Update/><ref name=NZH>{{cite news |last=Dann |first=Jennifer |date=9 October 2015 |title=12 Questions with Juliet Gerrard, Prime Minister's science advisor  |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12138857 |work=[[New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=6 April 2019}}</ref>

She is divorced<ref name=":0" /> and has two children.<ref name="NZH" />
